findings.specText: story-047: "AYieldStrategy: add setAsideBufferRecipient storage, SetAsideBufferRecipientSet event, and onlyOwner setSetAsideBufferRecipient setter (zero-address validated) ... ERC4626YieldStrategy: rework _distributeBuffer() to single aggregate transfer to recipient; add loud revert guard when totalBufferShares > 0 and recipient is unset. ERC4626MarketYieldStrategy: identical changes kept in sync."
findings.actualBehavior: All criteria verified at ad12cb1. Storage src/AYieldStrategy.sol:62; event :116-121; setter with require(_recipient != address(0)) :352-357; IYieldStrategy.sol declares setSetAsideBufferRecipient(address) and setAsideBufferRecipient() view (:141-153). Both concretes: loud guard ERC4626YieldStrategy.sol:245-248 / ERC4626MarketYieldStrategy.sol:291-294; per-client safeTransfer removed and replaced by single aggregate safeTransfer(setAsideBufferRecipient, totalSetAside) at ERC4626YieldStrategy.sol:323 / ERC4626MarketYieldStrategy.sol:368; both variants structurally identical. Zero-buffer back-compat preserved: the unbuffered fast path returns before the guard, so a skim with no configured buffers never reverts on an unset recipient.

(IYieldStrategy.sol:130-132)

findings.actualBehavior: Since story-047, the set-aside is NEVER returned to the client; it is summed across all clients and sent in one transfer to the global setAsideBufferRecipient (ERC4626YieldStrategy.sol:323, ERC4626MarketYieldStrategy.sol:368). An integrator reading setAsideBufferSize docs would wrongly conclude their contract receives its own buffer back.

findings.criterion: Law-1 override check: is shrinking the totalWithdrawal waiting period 24h->6h itself unsafe (rugpull-protection erosion)?
findings.specText: story-048: "change WAITING_PERIOD from 24h to 6h, EXECUTION_WINDOW from 48h to 72h"; rugpull-protection intent per AYieldStrategy.sol:415 "Provides community protection against rugpulls while allowing legitimate fund migrations"
findings.actualBehavior: Assessed and NOT escalated as an unsafe story. Rationale: (1) zero-delay owner exfiltration already exists via emergencyWithdraw (AYieldStrategy.sol:402, onlyOwner, no timelock, works while paused - known C-01), so the totalWithdrawal waiting period was never the binding rugpull protection; 6h vs 24h changes the marginal protection of a path that is already dominated by a 0h path. (2) Law 3 assumes a non-malicious owner; for the legitimate-migration use the story serves, 6h wait + 72h execution window (wider, more operationally forgiving than the old 48h) is a coherent trade. (3) The story is explicit and deliberate, not an accidental regression. Residual obligation: the centralization report text for C-01 and any user-facing docs citing a 24h reaction window must be updated to 6h (see FAITH-15-004) so the weaker posture is honestly disclosed - Law 1 recall is satisfied by keeping this assessment visible, not by inventing a High.
findings.deviation: none (blessed-by-story; doc disclosure handled in FAITH-15-004)

findings.criterion: Law-1 override + Law-3 footgun check: is redirecting ALL clients' set-aside buffers to one global recipient itself unsafe for non-recipient clients?
findings.specText: story-047: "redirect all set-aside buffers to single address"; setter NatSpec: "use this to direct buffer yield to a specific protocol address (e.g., stable-staker)" (AYieldStrategy.sol:344-346); superseded story-042 intent: "giving the client a reserve to absorb below-par dips"
findings.actualBehavior: Assessed and NOT escalated as an unsafe story: the redirected funds are realized SURPLUS only (principal accounting untouched, ERC4626YieldStrategy.sol:251 / ERC4626MarketYieldStrategy.sol:296), the redirect is explicit, loudly documented, and is the buffer-funding leg of the stable-staker integration - stable-staker's underwater exit path satisfies withdrawals from its on-contract buffer (lib/stable-staker/src/StableStaker.sol:780-790), which this recipient feeds. Legitimate design under the intended one-client-per-strategy deployment. RETAINED Law-3 FOOTGUN (Low, operational hazard): in a multi-client deployment where more than one client has a nonzero setAsideBufferSize, every non-recipient client's dip-absorption reserve is silently routed to the single recipient; a non-recipient client protocol whose underwater-exit machinery depends on receiving its own buffer back (story-042 semantics, still promised by the stale NatSpec flagged in FAITH-15-003) will find its underwater withdrawals reverting for lack of buffer. The consequence is non-obvious because the per-client setSetAsideBuffer setter still reads as a per-client reserve. Safe config: set nonzero buffers only for the client that is (or funnels to) setAsideBufferRecipient; document that buffers are protocol-level yield routing, not client reserves. Cross-protocol note for the next stable-staker run: buffer tokens arrive on StableStaker as idle balance, which StableStaker's owner rescue explicitly treats as fully rescuable when a strategy is set (StableStaker.sol:797-805) - rescuing the 'idle buffer' unknowingly removes the underwater-exit reserve this story exists to fund.
findings.deviation: none (blessed-by-story; footgun surfaced as operational hazard per Law 3)

findings.criterion: Ledger cross-check: does story-047 satisfy or advance F-03 (52f9b84a, run-14: stable-staker M-05 integration assumption for relinquishPrincipal wiring)?
findings.specText: F-03 (reports/ledgers/reflax-yield-vault.json): "caller MUST pay-out/write-off principal to its end user BEFORE calling relinquishPrincipal and MUST NOT re-credit the resulting reflax surplus to the same owner"; F-03 lawBasis recorded "Forward-looking with NO callsite at this commit"
findings.actualBehavior: Proposed F-03 disposition: KEEP OPEN, update annotation. Story-047 is a DIFFERENT leg of the stable-staker M-05 program (it funds the consumer-side buffer with skimmed surplus); it does not add, modify, or exercise any relinquishPrincipal callsite in reflax, so it neither satisfies nor violates F-03's invariant. However, F-03's recorded premise ('no callsite at this commit') is now STALE on the consumer side: lib/stable-staker/src/StableStaker.sol:786 (_routeExit underwater path) now calls strategy.relinquishPrincipal(token, amount) immediately before the caller pays the user from the on-contract buffer. Whether that wiring honors the pay-out-then-relinquish / no-double-credit invariant is a stable-staker-side conformance question and must be checked in the next stable-staker regression run, where F-03's Medium re-evaluation gate fires. Recommend: /ledger reflax-yield-vault annotate F-03 with the live callsite reference and a cross-project re-check trigger; do not close.
findings.deviation: none (disposition proposal, not a code deviation)
